A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments on Earth/climate data, meshes, SO(10), alanine dipeptide and robot trajectories, including quality, runtime and constraint-violation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional component ablations and trajectory diagnostics in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: Remark 5 adds an implicit-landing variant that evaluates the correction at the tangential proposal and adapts the landing rate. V2 also corrects landing, curvature and noise factors in the reported update formulas and Algorithms 1–2. The core OLLA/ULLA framework and CWPM objectives remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Earth/climate, mesh, SO(10), alanine and robot-trajectory tasks. The new component studies use retained datasets and constraints without adding a population, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same comparator membership and Appendix E.1 retains the same baseline procedures. V1 already discusses OLLA and the projection variants as failing on mixed tasks; v2's additional comparisons quantify these existing variants without introducing a new baseline.

E3.justification: V1 Table 7 and v2 Table 10 differ substantially: Earth/climate underdamped friction changes from 3 to 5 and maximum noise from 1.3 to 2.0; SO(10) networks change from width 512/depth 3 to 1024/5, alongside revised horizons, refresh frequencies and other settings. New ablations introduce component controls, violation AUC and projection-failure measurements. These reported revisions do not establish that retained benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds explicit studies of projection overhead, OLLA versus ULLA on alanine, curvature corrections and terminal projection, plus trajectory-wise violation diagnostics. These substantially expand component and feasibility analysis. The earlier alpha/epsilon sensitivity results remain in Appendix E.4.

E5.justification: Both retain five independent runs with mean ± standard error in Table 1 and the existing uncertainty reporting in Table 3 and the alpha/epsilon ablations. V2 adds no seed information, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedure; its new component tables provide point estimates.

E6.justification: Main benchmark Tables 1–3 and the full alpha/epsilon results retain their values, but v2 adds substantial component results. Table 4 newly reports ULLA versus ULLA-P inference times of 0.13 versus 1.13 ms/sample and failure rates of 0% versus 20%. Tables 5–7 and Figure 4 add dynamics, correction, terminal-projection and trajectory-feasibility findings.

T1.justification: V2 adds Lemma A.1 and its explicit/implicit residual proof, corrects underdamped transition-density normalization in Appendix C, and repairs conditional Wasserstein inequalities and covariance factors in Appendix D. Lemma D.2 replaces the earlier second-moment argument with augmented scaled-pair moments, all-order source-moment assumptions and an extensive propagation proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, unified-constraint contribution and claimed speedups remain. The introduction qualifies its feasibility claim: continuous-time dynamics preserve feasibility from feasible initialization, whereas discretization provides self-correction with optional terminal projection. This narrows the earlier unqualified wording about maintaining feasibility along the path.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of momentum reducing boundary re-entry, the limited empirical benefit of curvature corrections, and terminal projection primarily improving residual precision. It explicitly discusses discrete near-feasibility, O(dN) trajectory-storage costs and biased component coverage from inadequate priors on disconnected feasible sets.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer, identifies which experiments use implicit landing, and specifies terminal-projection use by task. The revised hyperparameter table, corrected pseudocode and new alpha/epsilon tuning guidance materially strengthen implementation documentation. Repository availability itself cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The same distinct prior works and research positioning are retained. Changes update publication metadata, correct author information and consolidate duplicate references, including the Christopher et al. entries.

P1.justification: V2 introduces a dedicated component-ablation subsection, rewrites the conclusion to include limitations and future work, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Local language, terminology and bibliographic edits accompany these changes; most exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds four compact ablation tables and a trajectory-violation plot, refines Table 3 highlighting and captions, and removes the redundant main-text alpha/epsilon summary. Its full results remain in the appendix as Table 11. Existing benchmark displays and the overall visual format are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects substantive errors in the mathematical justification and supplies direct component tests for previously weakly supported efficiency and feasibility explanations. Clearer implementation disclosures and limitations further improve reproducibility and claim precision. The revised theory requires explicit higher-moment assumptions, and changed settings do not establish benchmark reruns, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial gains in rigor and empirical support.
